```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Load the runner tracking data and the steal attempt summary data.
# runner_tracks contains frame-level runner positions.
# steal_attempts contains one row per steal attempt with play information.

source("SMT_Data_Starter.R")
runner_tracks <- readRDS("runner_tracks.rds")
steal_attempts <- readRDS("steal_attempts.rds")
```

## Gathering instantaneous speeds of runners

```{r}
# Calculate runner speed at each timestamp within each individual steal attempt.
# The data is arranged by game, play, and time so that lag() compares each frame to the previous frame in the same play.


runner_tracks <- runner_tracks %>%
  arrange(game_string, play_per_game, timestamp) %>%
  group_by(game_string, play_per_game) %>%
  mutate(
# dt is the time difference between consecutive frames, converted from milliseconds to seconds.
    dt = (timestamp - lag(timestamp)) / 1000,
# dx and dy measure how far the runner moved in the x and y directions between frames.
    dx = field_x - lag(field_x),
    dy = field_y - lag(field_y),
# Speed is calculated as distance traveled divided by time elapsed.
    speed = sqrt(dx^2 + dy^2) / dt
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

## Top speeds during each play:

```{r}
# Calculate a top-speed metric for each steal attempt.
# Instead of taking one single maximum speed reading, this uses a one-second rolling average.
# That makes the metric more stable and reduces the impact of one noisy tracking frame.

top_speed <- runner_tracks %>%
  filter(!is.na(speed), is.finite(speed)) %>%
  arrange(game_string, play_per_game, timestamp) %>%
  group_by(game_string, play_per_game) %>%
  mutate(
# For each timestamp, calculate the average runner speed over the previous one second.
    speed_1sec_avg = slider::slide_index_dbl(
      .x = speed,
      .i = timestamp,
      .f = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
      .before = 1000,
      .complete = TRUE
    )
  ) %>%
  summarize(
# The top speed for the play is the highest one-second rolling average.
    top_speed = max(speed_1sec_avg, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Add the top-speed metric back onto the steal attempt table.
# any_of() removes an older top_speed column if the chunk has already been run before.

steal_attempts <- steal_attempts %>%
  select(-any_of("top_speed")) %>%
  left_join(
    top_speed,
    by = c("game_string", "play_per_game")
  )
```

# Keeping only first few tenths of a second to look at jumps

```{r}
# Create a time variable measured relative to pitch release.
# This lets the jump metric focus on the runner's first 0.4 seconds after the pitch is released.

runner_tracks <- runner_tracks %>%
  mutate(
    time_since_pitch =
      (timestamp - pitch_timestamp)/1000
  )
```

# Jump metric:

```{r}
# Calculate the runner's jump for each steal attempt.
# Jump is defined as the runner's speed around 0.4 seconds after pitch release minus the runner's speed at pitch release.
# A larger value means the runner gained speed more quickly at the start of the steal attempt.

jump_metric <- runner_tracks %>%
  filter(
    time_since_pitch >= 0,
    time_since_pitch <= 0.4
  ) %>%
  group_by(game_string, play_per_game) %>%
  summarize(
# Runner speed closest to the moment of pitch release.
    speed_at_release = speed[which.min(abs(time_since_pitch))],
# Runner speed closest to 0.4 seconds after pitch release.
    speed_at_0_4 = speed[which.min(abs(time_since_pitch - 0.4))],
# Jump is the amount of speed gained in the first 0.4 seconds.
    jump = speed_at_0_4 - speed_at_release,
    .groups = "drop"
  )
# Add the jump metric back onto the steal attempt table.
# The select() line removes previous jump columns to avoid duplicate names after re-running the chunk.
steal_attempts <- steal_attempts %>%
  select(-any_of(c("jump", "jump.x", "jump.y"))) %>%
  left_join(
    jump_metric,
    by = c("game_string", "play_per_game")
  )
```

## Setting up data for future use:

```{r}
## Save clean runner metrics

# runner_info is the clean runner-side file for the final leaderboard maker.
# It contains one row per steal attempt with the runner metrics already calculated.

# Create a clean dataset with only the runner-side information needed later.
# This file is used by the leaderboard and modeling scripts.

runner_info <- steal_attempts %>%
  mutate(
# Convert play_per_game to numeric so it joins cleanly with other play-level files later.
    play_per_game = as.numeric(play_per_game)
  ) %>%
  select(
    game_string,
    play_per_game,
    runner,
    catcher,
    outcome,
    top_speed,
    jump
  ) %>%
  filter(
# Keep only plays with a known outcome and valid runner metrics.
    !is.na(outcome),
    !is.na(top_speed),
    !is.na(jump)
  )
# Save the cleaned runner metrics so the next files can load them directly.
saveRDS(runner_info, "runner_info.rds")
```
